solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unable to get on topic, men bail out

indicators.note: something put out is thrown into disorder, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: twelve letters taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Stuck on a dull subject, the men abandon the discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unable to get on topic' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'get on', meaning to have a good relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: People described this way cannot live or work together harmoniously, which is exactly failing to rub along.

clue.text: They cover Poles in charge of room facing north

indicators.note: in a down clue, pointing north means reading upward, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge
room as in space to move

explanation.surface: Someone supervising the Polish workers in a north-facing room.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P makes 'Poles' look like people from Poland; they are the Earth's North and South Poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Permanent sheets of frozen water blanket the Arctic and Antarctic regions, sitting over the planet's two extreme points.

clue.text: Dearth of screws spoiled clothing unit

indicators.note: something spoiled has been ruined or messed up, so the letters lose their original order

blocks.note: fourteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A flat-pack wardrobe ruined because the kit came without enough screws.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a furniture-assembly grumble, which makes the answer almost part of the story.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of bedroom furniture with sliding compartments, used for storing garments, is a unit for clothes.

clue.text: Drive second to right

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An instruction to steer the car one second towards the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like an ordinal but is the noun meaning a brief moment, informally a mo.
explanation.definitionFit: To travel by car is an old-fashioned verb sense, as in motoring down to the coast.

clue.text: Sort of farmer employing cook for fetching

indicators.note: to employ something is to take it on and hold it within, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: an arable farmer grows crops rather than keeping livestock
to do food is to cook it, as in doing the vegetables

explanation.surface: A farmer who hires a cook to go and get things for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fetching' looks like the verb to fetch; it is the adjective meaning attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something charming and attractive, a delightful appearance that wins people over.

clue.text: Capri for one is nearly all rented out

indicators.note: nearly all of something falls just short of the whole, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
property rented out is let

explanation.surface: Holiday homes on Capri are almost all rented out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a whole island's housing is taken; 'nearly all' trims the word for rented out.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is a small island in the Bay of Naples, an example of a poetic word for island.

clue.text: Maximum efforts make flat worst!

blocks.note: a flat surface is level
as a verb, to worst someone is to defeat them, which is also to best them

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry that trying one's hardest has only made things worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worst' looks like the superlative of bad, the opposite of what it gives; as a verb it means to defeat, and so does its apparent opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing one's utmost is an idiom for trying as hard as possible, giving everything.

clue.text: Pelican alongside zebra? That’s cheating

blocks.note: first meaning: pelican and zebra crossings are British pedestrian crossings, and two side by side make a pair of them
second meaning: betraying someone you are supposedly working with

explanation.surface: A pelican trying to pass itself off beside a zebra is caught out cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a zebra crossing is a striped pedestrian crossing and a pelican crossing is a light-controlled one, so the two animals are road crossings, not creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceiving a partner by secretly working against them is treachery, a form of dishonest dealing.

clue.text: Shelter a poor area bringing in yen

indicators.note: to bring something in is to take it inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: taken as written
a slum is a run-down poor district
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A refuge in a deprived district is funded with Japanese money.
explanation.walkthrough: Y is the currency symbol for the yen, a standard abbreviation worth learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Protection given to someone fleeing danger, especially a refugee granted sanctuary by a foreign state.

clue.text: Assemble before empty court

indicators.note: an empty thing has lost its contents, so only the shell of outer letters remains

blocks.note: ere is a poetic word for before
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: People gathering ahead of a courtroom session with no one in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assemble' suggests gathering people; here it means to build, and ERE is the poetic word for before.
explanation.definitionFit: To put up a structure is to build it or put it together, as with scaffolding.

clue.text: Unaware, left island blocking patent

indicators.note: a blockage sits in the middle of a passage, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: patent as an adjective means plain to see
L is the abbreviation for left
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Someone who departed an island without realising they were infringing a patent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patent' looks like the legal noun for an invention right; here it is the adjective meaning evident.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking any awareness of what is happening around them is completely heedless of it.

clue.text: Antenna limits radio telephony along major roads

definitions.note: adjectival phrase; the answer is an adjective describing main routes

indicators.note: limits are boundaries on either side, so the outer word encloses the other

blocks.note: a radio or TV aerial is an antenna
RT is the abbreviation for radio telephony

explanation.surface: A mast restricts radio phone signals along the motorway network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limits' reads as a verb meaning restricts; here the antenna word forms the outer boundaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic arteries are the main routes of a network, so an adjective for trunk roads carrying heavy through-traffic.

clue.text: Miss transporting large old bishop everywhere

definitions.note: an adverb; the answer is an adjective meaning happening everywhere

indicators.note: to transport something is to carry it, so one piece holds the others inside

blocks.note: a miss is a young woman, informally a gal
L is the abbreviation for large, as in clothing sizes
O is the abbreviation for old
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A young woman carrying a large, elderly bishop all over the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' could be a verb meaning to fail to hit; it is the title for a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worldwide extends across the whole planet, found in every place.

clue.text: Game frequently interrupts society dance

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so this piece goes inside

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for society
oft is an old word for often
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A sporting match keeps breaking up a society dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The inserted piece goes between the society abbreviation and the dance, which together make the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sport resembling baseball, played with a larger ball pitched underarm, is one example of a team sport.

clue.text: Make mess of most of top pitch

indicators.note: most of something is all except a little, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: to top is to beat, which is to best
a sales pitch is a salesman's patter

explanation.surface: Churning up the best part of the playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' suggests a football field; it is the smooth talk of a salesperson.
explanation.definitionFit: To splash something all over with mud or dirt is to soil it by spattering.

clue.text: Save visibly embarrassed Europeans getting married

blocks.note: an embarrassed person goes red in the face
E is the abbreviation for European, doubled for the plural
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: Blushing continentals get hitched to spare themselves further shame.
explanation.walkthrough: Europeans gives two Es, one per person, since E is the standard abbreviation for European.
explanation.definitionFit: In a religious or rescuing sense, delivering someone from sin or harm, as a saviour does.

clue.text: Small pot preserving queen’s tooth

indicators.note: to preserve something is to keep it safe inside, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
in snooker, to pot a ball is to pocket it
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A little jar keeping the Queen's tooth as a relic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot' looks like a noun for a jar; it is the snooker verb. The 's on queen is 'queen is', so the queen sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Each projecting cog on a wheel that engages a chain is called by this name, a tooth on a gear.

clue.text: Teacher ignoring note put weight on

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so letters are removed

blocks.note: a schoolmistress is a female teacher
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A teacher taking no notice of a note and piling on the pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put weight on' suggests gaining pounds; here it means to emphasise.
explanation.definitionFit: To give emphasis to a point is to lay importance on it, figuratively loading it.

clue.text: Win over French nobleman in match

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: in poker, to see a bet is to match it
duc is French for duke

explanation.surface: Beating a French aristocrat in a sporting contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like a contest noun; it is the poker verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm or tempt someone into doing something is to persuade them, attracting them to your side.

clue.text: Johnny-come-latelies stumped in high-class roles

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
actors' roles are parts
st is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

explanation.surface: Newcomers baffled when cast as posh characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stumped' looks like baffled; it is a way of being out in cricket, where the wicketkeeper breaks the stumps, abbreviated ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Newly arrived people who have risen quickly and act above their station are recent arrivals resented by the established.

clue.text: Setting time‘s free in most quarters

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: three of the four compass points, south, west and north
to free a knot is to undo it

explanation.surface: Leisure hours are available in most parts of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setting time' reads as fixing a clock; it is the time the sun sets. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening, when the sun sinks below the horizon, is the moment of sunset.

clue.text: Some hide mate married on the rebound

indicators.note: a rebound sends a thing back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a mate is a friend, a pal
wed is a verb and adjective for married

explanation.surface: Someone concealing that their friend has married on the rebound from a breakup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like the verb to conceal; it is the noun for skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The loose fold of skin hanging from the throat of cattle is a portion of an animal's skin.

clue.text: One wearing medals running funny business

indicators.note: the wearer surrounds whatever is worn, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
gongs is informal British slang for medals or honours
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: A decorated officer in a race is up to something suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: Gongs is informal British slang for medals or honours, and running means working, as a machine is on.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspicious or improper activity, shady behaviour that people gossip about, is the sense here.

clue.text: Finish off standard musical work

indicators.note: to finish something off here is to take its finish, its end, away

blocks.note: normal means standard or usual

explanation.surface: Completing a conventional piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish off' reads as complete; here it means chop off the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellini's opera about a Druid priestess is a well-known piece of operatic repertoire.

clue.text: Hum very loudly after returning home

indicators.note: something returning comes back the way it went, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: someone at home is in
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Humming at full volume after getting back to the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hum' looks like singing with closed lips; in British slang a hum is a bad smell, and so is a niff.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words for an unpleasant odour, a stink.

clue.text: Find the lady maybe, daughter hiding in trailer with haystack

indicators.note: a thing hiding in another is tucked inside it

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
a cart is a trailer pulled behind a horse or tractor
a rick is a stack of hay

explanation.surface: Searching for a woman whose daughter is hiding in a hay trailer, like a needle in a haystack.
explanation.walkthrough: Find the lady is the three-card game where a sharper shuffles three cards and you must spot the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-card con in which you guess where the queen lies is one example of sleight-of-hand with playing cards.

clue.text: It may charge money

blocks.note: first meaning: a large horned animal that rushes at threats
second meaning: old British slang for cash

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a shop charging a fee; the charge is an animal's attack, and the second meaning is dated British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The African beast famously stampedes at intruders, and the same word is old slang for cash.

clue.text: Divert RAF importing what keeps firm afloat

indicators.note: to divert is to send off in another direction, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Redirecting the Royal Air Force's imports to save a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Importing' looks like a container signal, but it is part of the fodder along with the three letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The gap between revenue and costs is what lets a business stay solvent and in operation.
